summary: This program picks a game level name from a number using the ternary operator, Java's compact one-line alternative to an if/else chain. With levelNumber set to 17 it prints "intermediate".

lines.code: int levelNumber = 17; // change this value to test
lines.text: The whole program hinges on this one number, so change it to 5 or 25 and re-run to watch each branch fire in turn.

Unlike an if statement, a ternary is an expression: it evaluates to a value, which is why it can sit on the right of an assignment. Read the ? as "then" — if the test is true the whole expression becomes "novice".
The colon means "otherwise", and what follows here is a second ternary nested inside the first. This chaining is the ternary equivalent of else if.
Every ternary needs a final else branch, so this bare value catches everything 20 and above. Because it is only reached after the earlier tests failed, no lower bound needs stating.
Storing the result in level first and printing it afterwards keeps the decision and the output separate, which is easier to read than burying the ternary inside the println call.
